gloss: Sen no Rikyū (1522-1591), master of the tea ceremony

definitions.explanation: A merchant from Sakai who became tea master to {織田信長|おだのぶなが} and {豊臣秀吉|とよとみひでよし} and perfected the style of tea known as わび{茶|ちゃ}, which values simplicity and quiet, rustic beauty. Hideyoshi later ordered him to commit suicide, for reasons still debated.

examples.japanese: {千利休|せんのりきゅう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{大成|たいせい}した。
examples.english: Sen no Rikyū perfected the way of tea.

examples.japanese: {利休|りきゅう}はわび⟦{茶|ちゃ}→茶：03433_cha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{美|び}→美：28891_bi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{追求|ついきゅう}→追求：14401_tsuikyuu⟧した。
examples.english: Rikyū pursued the beauty of wabi tea.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{表千家|おもてせんけ}→表千家：30917_omotesenke⟧や⟦{裏千家|うらせんけ}→裏千家：30918_urasenke⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、どちらも{利休|りきゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子孫|しそん}→子孫：00372_shison⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ→受け継ぐ：06700_uketsugu⟧⟦{流派|りゅうは}→流派：13365_ryuuha⟧だ。
examples.english: Today's Omotesenke and Urasenke are both schools passed down by Rikyū's descendants.

notes:
Rikyū is the central figure of the tea ceremony; the three main {千家|せんけ} schools trace their line to him. His name is also used for things in a simple, understated style.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- わび⟦{茶|ちゃ}→茶：03433_cha⟧: the austere, rustic style of tea he perfected
- ⟦{一期一会|いちごいちえ}→一期一会：04768_ichigoichie⟧: "one time, one meeting" — the tea-ceremony ideal that each gathering is unique, traced to his teaching
- {待庵|たいあん}: the two-mat tea room attributed to him, a national treasure
- {利休|りきゅう}⟦{鼠|ねずみ}→鼠：02238_nezumi⟧: a gray with a green tint named after him

CULTURAL NOTE:
His contrast with Hideyoshi, who built a golden tea room, is a favorite theme of novels and films about taste and power.
